name: shelf
words: how a body reads the shelf, the wear table and the draft shelf, and how a human cuts a craft — the Orreth skill for THE SHELF WIDENED (Phase 8 sp2)
text: THE SHELF holds every service the kernel governs (tool, mcp, store, source, mind — each a self with a DID) AND every craft a body is made of (template, prompt, skill, policy, graph, binding, golden — each addressed by name and pin, never a self). A craft's shelf name is <name>.<kind> (librarian.template, mind.v0.graph, librarian.golden); its address is craft:<name>.<kind>. One ladder for all: registered -> versioned(n) -> healthy | unhealthy -> retired, restore returns it. A craft is healthy when its declaration reads whole; a template is healthy only when its graph stands on the shelf. GET /services lists them (?kind= filters); a craft row carries `craft` (its bare name) and `worn_by` (how many bodies wear it now). THE WEAR TABLE (GET /wear): which body wears which component at which version — written by the body in its join's transaction (template, binding, policy, graph, golden), the previous life's rows closed; ?component=<shelf name> answers who wears it ('in use by N' — the blast radius a change would touch); ?did= answers what a body is made of. THE DRAFT SHELF (GET/POST /drafts): a draft lives in the ground under the PERSON who wrote it; only their seat reads it; it is never on the shelf, never in any listing or recall (AG-9). Saving a draft is routine (L1) — no fact. THE CUT (POST /drafts/cut) is the gate: the kernel holds `craft.cut` at the interlock — L2 for most crafts, L3 (the code) for a resident's template; firmware is cut only in a dev universe (prod reaches it as a release); an agent's template waits for the Experiment (spoonful 4). On the human's yes the draft lands as a registered craft (version 1) or the next version of one already there, the person on the chain, and the draft is spent. THE HULL: every body runs hear -> recall -> route -> chat | work | event -> the work node, which runs its template's `graph` component from the shelf (mind.v0 = the metered think, echo.v0 = the words back); the edge is read off the ask's marker (a human's ask is chat; an intention's occurrence is work; a marker of interest is an event) and named in the journey. In the glass: 'show the crafts', 'show the templates', 'who wears the librarian template?', 'what is echo made of?', 'my drafts', 'draft a prompt called greeting: Greet the human by name.', 'cut the greeting draft', 'discard the greeting draft', 'retire the greeting prompt', 'restore the greeting prompt'. A body never cuts, retires or restores a craft itself — only the kernel does, on a person's word; say the exact words the human can say.
